title: Vendor Onboarding: SOC2 Evidence Pack & Insurance Verification Playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
Create a lightweight, operational playbook that standardizes how Redwood evaluates and accepts vendor SOC2 evidence, insurance certificates, and vendor portal artifacts for enterprise contracts. This playbook will be used by PMs, Solutions, Legal, and Security to reduce deal friction, ensure consistent risk posture, and speed procurement cycles for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Scope & Goals:
- Define the minimum SOC2 evidence bundle we accept (Type II report, AOC, complementary user-entity controls mapping, management response summary).
- Create standard insurance minimums (E&O, Cyber, limits, retroactive dates) and a quick verification checklist for Risk team.
- Map common vendor security questionnaire items (SIG, CAIQ, custom RFI) to one-page canned responses maintained by Security.
- Produce a templated email/playbook for Solutions/Account teams to request missing artifacts and follow SLAs.
- Identify which steps can be automated (doc ingestion into vendor-portal, expiry alerts, redlineable contract clauses).

Acceptance criteria (must be met before rolling out to GTM):
- Playbook doc authored in Confluence with clear owner, versioning, and rollback instructions.
- SOC2 minimum evidence checklist with examples and red flags.
- Insurance verification template with sample acceptable certificates.
- One-page canned responses for the top 20 questionnaire items.
- Internal training run for Sales and Legal (30 min) with slide deck and FAQ.
- Automation backlog created and prioritized (at least 2 automations scoped).

Planned deliverables & timeline:
- Week 0 (now): Draft checklist and insurance template (owner: Liam).
- Week 1: Security review and iteration (owner: Nadia - Security).
- Week 2: Legal signoff and create canned responses (owner: Priya - Legal).
- Week 3: Confluence publish, internal training, and handoff to Solutions.

Stakeholders and SMEs:
- Product Management: Asha (owner), Liam (assignee)
- Security: Nadia Brooks (SOC2 evidence mapping)
- Legal: Priya Ram (contract and insurance language)
- Sales/Solutions: Marco Silva (GTM enablement)
- Engineering: ENG-1899 (automation feasibility)

Known trade-offs and decisions to make:
- Tightening insurance minima may slow deals in APAC where local carriers differ. We'll propose an exceptions flow.
- We will accept SOC2 Type II plus AOC as baseline; Type I accepted only on a case-by-case basis for small partners.
- Full questionnaire completion will not be required for low-risk vendors; we will enumerate risk tiers.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Vendors provide stale SOC2 artifacts. Mitigation: require report date + management attestation dated within 12 months; add expiry tracking.
- Risk: Legal overhead for non-standard clauses. Mitigation: maintain pre-approved fallback clauses and white-list negotiable items.

Links & artifacts:
- Draft playbook (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENT/pages/56321/Vendor+Onboarding+Playbook
- Sample SOC2 AOC (drive): https://drive.rewood.example/soc2-samples
- PR for automation spike: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2498

Next steps (actionable items):
- Liam to post draft playbook and ping Security for review by 2025-02-17.
- Nadia to assemble canned responses and mark high-risk questionnaire fields by 2025-02-19.
- Priya to draft insurance language and exceptions process by 2025-02-20.
- Schedule 30-min GTM training on 2025-02-24.
